_header: This fixture pins the EXACT `shed sessions --json` document the ROOST path
produces (plan 022 C5c): a FLAT array, one entry per row, in the same order the
table prints -- per shed, the roost tabs and then the tmux rows.
What it exists to catch: a renamed, dropped, added or reordered key. The array
is what scripts read, and the C5c rule is that it stays ADDITIVE -- a tmux entry
is byte-for-byte the config.Session it always was, plus "source":"tmux"; a roost
entry borrows that same shape ("name" is the TAB TITLE, which is what
`shed sessions kill <shed> <name>` takes) and nests everything roost-specific
under "roost". Consumed by cmd/shed/sessions_roost_test.go:
TestSessionsJSONGolden, which feeds `listings` to mergedSessionRows and compares
the compacted marshalling against `want_json`.
Two shapes are deliberately visible here and neither is a bug:
- a roost row's "attached" is always false and its "window_count" is absent --
a tab has neither, and its liveness is roost.state, not a second answer;
- a tab from an older session carries no created_at and no agent_lifecycle, so
it serializes as the zero time and an empty "agent". The CREATED column
renders that as `unknown`.
The tmux FLOOR (--tmux / SHED_ATTACH=tmux / no local roost) is NOT this shape:
it prints today's bare config.Session array with no "source" key at all, which
TestSessionsJSONFloorHasNoSourceKey pins separately.
If a change to the rendering makes this go red, the fix is almost always in that
new code, not in this fixture -- an array key is somebody's script.

scenarios.name: roost_tab_then_tmux_row
scenarios.doc: one shed with a tab shed opened (titled and locked) and a tmux session of the same name: the tab comes first, both carry their source

scenarios.name: two_servers_and_an_older_session
scenarios.doc: the fleet shape: sheds ordered by (server, shed), a shed whose only rows are roost tabs, a shed whose only rows are tmux sessions, and a tab from a session that reports neither created_at nor agent_lifecycle
